items.title: Live GitHub Copilot model-catalog check (/gsd copilot-models)
items.context: Adds a GSD-extension-side /gsd copilot-models command that fetches GET /models from the authenticated GitHub Copilot account, sanitizes and diffs against a last-known-good snapshot, and dedupes shell notifications, without mutating provider registration, routing, policy, or credentials. Reuses existing registry/OAuth seams (packages/pi-ai github-copilot OAuth, model-registry). Scoped as GSD-extension-only per CONTRIBUTING.md's scope-area table; not auto-mode, so no RFC required. Branch hygiene fixed: re-based off a fresh upstream/main worktree/branch (feat/github-copilot-model-catalog-sync) instead of the retired fix/mai-cost-table-provider-section, which is left untouched as historical GSD-W011 reference only. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this is a manual, session-scoped, read-only drift-check only — a first slice of the fuller catalog-sync vision (provider-owned live catalog refresh, router integration, automatic cost-table updates, interactive drift signaling) described in this feature's own local execution plan, not the complete feature. Do not present this entry as covering that fuller scope.
items.validation: Ported cleanly (git am, no conflicts) onto fresh upstream/main (09ae3c22c3286d3e988ccb94cee27279e026b329). 15/15 targeted unit tests pass (copilot-model-catalog.test.ts, copilot-models-handler.test.ts, ADR-012 provider-equality-allowlist) and typecheck:extensions is clean against the current architecture. Earlier local pnpm run verify:pr and remote CI totals (14176 passed/0 failed/31 skipped) were measured against the prior commit on the retired branch and remain informative but are not re-verified against this new branch's exact HEAD.
items.nextAction: Do not open an issue or PR without explicit authorization. Before any PR: (1) decide and document whether the drift-check slice ships as the whole feature or whether router/cost-table/interactive-signaling work continues first; (2) confirm whether CONTRIBUTING.md rule 3 (issue-first for new features) applies (likely yes — the first-time-contributor exemption no longer applies since PR #1758/GSD-W011 is merged, but this is a new feature, not an obvious bug fix). Branch is pushed to pimmink/gsd-pi as a WIP backup only, not for review.

items.title: Sharded remote pr-verification harness (test-efficiency workstream)
items.context: Lives entirely in the separate, fully user-owned pimmink/gsd-pi-ci harness repository, not in pimmink/gsd-pi — no upstream/fork PR is applicable. Adds .github/workflows/remote-pr-verification-sharded.yml, an experimental workflow_dispatch-only workflow that splits pimmink/gsd-pi's test:unit:compiled across 4 parallel shards using Node's native --test-shard=<index>/<total>, after independently validating locally (synthetic multi-glob fixture, exact production flag combination) that the flag must be placed before the glob patterns and is deterministic/complete/non-overlapping. Left the stable remote-pr-verification.yml completely untouched.
items.validation: Two real dispatches against pimmink/gsd-pi commit 28a2c92c3835e61f5fd19beffc6b8b4c6476bfc6 (fix/mai-cost-table-provider-section, historical GSD-W011/W014 spike commit, used only as a fixed measurement target). First dispatch (run 32015752880) failed fast and safely at an intentional file-count safety check (1274 actual vs an incorrectly hand-counted 1272 expected) before any shard ran. Corrective dispatch (run 32016308055) succeeded: all 4 shards + lifecycle-gate + aggregate green; aggregate totals across shards exactly matched the known unsharded baseline (14176 passed/0 failed/31 skipped), proving no test file was skipped or duplicated; total wall clock ~12m04s vs the 19m11s unsharded baseline (~37% reduction, run 31857969918). Merged to gsd-pi-ci:main (fast-forward, no PR needed for this private single-owner repo).
items.nextAction: None required to consider this workstream done. Optional future follow-up: consider promoting the sharded workflow from experimental to the primary remote-pr-verification path once used a few more times, and revisit shard_count if the real suite's size/composition changes materially.
